articles.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
articles.summary: Personalization is essential for general-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction. articles.title: Which Tokens to Merge? Diffusion Dynamics for Efficient Image Generation
articles.summary: Token merging has emerged as an effective training-free strategy for accelerating diffusion models by reducing redundant token computation while minimizing generation degradation. A key challenge is determining which tokens can be safely merged and which should be preserved for subsequent computation. articles.title: SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers
articles.summary: Diffusion and flow models generate a sample over iterative steps, each a full pass through a large network, and that pass dominates generation cost. Training-free caching accelerates them by reusing activations from recent evaluations instead of recomputing them. articles.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
articles.summary: Significant efforts are currently being directed toward the implementation of large-scale quantum information processors, but realizing useful quantum advantage also requires the development of efficient quantum algorithms. While for many practical problems the dominant resource costs are associated with a small set of computational primitives, optimizing them in the quantum setting presents unique challenges, including a reversibility constraint absent from ordinary classical computation. articles.summary: We construct semiclassical 3D models based on $\textit{ab initio}$ no-core shell model calculated two-body spatial correlations, which represent the preferred spatial configuration of nucleons for the ground state of $^6$He. articles.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
articles.summary: Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human-defined environmental rules. We introduce T2-Z for test-time optimization of environment latents, which augments a robotic world model with a learnable environment latent to condition world predictions. articles.title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
articles.summary: Generative simulation can automate robot environment construction, but physically valid environments are not necessarily useful for training. The challenge is to identify environments that address a policy's failures and supervision that helps it overcome them. We introduce CoDA, a framework in which a simulation data engine and an action policy co-evolve through a shared heterogeneous memory of environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress. articles.title: Grounding Generative Verification in 3D Content
articles.summary: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and 3D generation have expanded 3D understanding and synthesis. However, beyond visual fidelity, task-specific correctness grounded in 3D evidence remains a major challenge. We argue that building reliable 3D systems requires not only stronger generation and reasoning, but also verification feedback that identifies unmet requirements and explains their violations, allowing systems to reflect on and refine their outputs. articles.summary: We establish Iritani's integral form of the $\mathbb{C}^\times$-equivariant Crepant Transformation Conjecture (CTC) for the minimal resolution of the surface singularity $\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{BD}_{4n}$, where $\mathbb{BD}_{4n}$ is the binary dihedral group of order $4n$. articles.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
articles.summary: Time series foundation models are becoming increasingly popular for general-purpose forecasting. However, most leading models predict marginal quantiles, leaving the dependence structure of future trajectories unspecified. This distinction matters for trajectory-dependent quantities such as cumulative demand, peak load, and event timing, yet point and marginal scores do not reveal it. articles.title: DK-VLM: Geometry as Position for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
articles.summary: Vision-language models still struggle to understand 3D spatial relations across views and update spatial judgments as the observer moves. A common approach fuses 3D reconstruction features into visual tokens, but aligning these features with pretrained semantic representations remains challenging under limited spatial supervision. articles.summary: Generative visual verifiers play a crucial role in advancing multimodal intelligence. articles.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
articles.summary: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models have become an important approach for scaling model parameters. Modern MoE architectures increasingly combine two design choices: fine-grained expert segmentation and shared experts. The former increases expressiveness by enabling more expert combinations at a fixed activation ratio, and the latter introduces experts that are active for every token. articles.title: SUPRA-TEX: 3D Generation with Super-Aligned Texture
articles.summary: Single image 3D generation aims to dress a given 3D mesh with relightable materials while faithfully preserving the visual details of a reference image. Existing methods either introduce artifacts when fusing inconsistent multi-view predictions or struggle to preserve fine details through implicit image-feature conditioning. articles.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
articles.summary: Existing agent benchmarks typically evaluate agents on well-specified tasks defined by issue reports, specifications, or task tickets. Real-world customer delivery is different: forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) must clarify ambiguous requirements, work in live systems, and uncover unstated constraints. articles.title: Singles in Disguise: Kepler's Low-SNR Single-Transiting Systems as Incompletely Detected Multis
articles.summary: NASA's Kepler mission found more systems with one transiting planet (``singles'') than expected from those with several (``multis''). This excess was first taken as evidence for a Kepler dichotomy -- a second population of intrinsically single or highly inclined systems -- but later work argued that selection effects acting on a single population can reproduce it. articles.title: Projected sensitivity of a spinor Bose-Einstein condensate comagnetometer to proton monopole-dipole interactions
articles.summary: Light spin-zero bosons with scalar and pseudoscalar couplings mediate a parity- and time-reversal-violating monopole-dipole interaction between unpolarized matter and polarized spins. articles.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
articles.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are expanding from assisting scientific research and engineering to autonomously developing and improving AI systems, advancing AI for AI (AI4AI) as a pathway toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). articles.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
articles.summary: Recent 3D world models increasingly use features from geometry foundation models (GFMs) as predictive world states, benefiting from their rich geometric priors. However, the view dependence of these features entangles scene dynamics with camera-induced variation, making the resulting state evolution harder to predict. articles.title: Spark-0: Scaling Spatially Aligned Tactile Pretraining for Robot Dexterous Manipulation
articles.summary: Generalist robot policies benefit from large-scale visual pretraining but often struggle with contact-rich dexterous manipulation, where force, compliance, and incipient slip are hard to observe from images. We present Spark-0, a spatially aligned vision-tactile-language-action (VTLA) model that uses touch in two complementary ways. articles.title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
articles.summary: We introduce 3DCodeVerse, a research ecosystem that enables coding agents to create editable and verifiable 3D content at scale. 3DCodeVerse comprises large-scale, high-quality datasets of executable 3D code, a coding harness for spatial reasoning and automated verification, and practical guidance for 3D coding. articles.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
articles.summary: How can robots autonomously collect the contact-rich experience needed to learn dexterous manipulation? We present DSP: Dexterity from supervised play, a framework in which a robot learns a play policy from minutes of human play through behavior cloning, then deploys it autonomously to collect hours of interaction data to train a world model. articles.title: Identifying deformed exoplanets with JWST and Ariel: A target selection metric for phase curve observations
articles.summary: The shape of an exoplanet encodes fundamental information about its internal structure. For close-in giant planets, strong stellar tidal forces induce measurable deformations that can be probed through high-precision photometry. articles.title: Robust Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Treatment Regimes under Model and Measurement Uncertainty
articles.summary: We develop a robust reinforcement learning (RL) framework for learning adaptive treatment policies that generalize across patients and remain reliable under errors in the measured biomarker and shifts in the disease dynamics. By modeling the patient as a hidden context, we address generalization and robustness in a unified manner through robust contextual Markov decision processes. articles.title: How Do Emotions Spread And Affect Decision-Making In Social Networks? An Opinion Dynamics Perspective
articles.summary: Emotions affect how we think and perceive information. Motivated by this, we present a novel framework for modeling emotions, and study its impact in social networks. We represent emotions on a circle by utilizing the circumplex model. articles.title: Illumination-Aware Active Perception for Spacecraft Inspection
articles.summary: Harsh and rapidly varying orbital illumination introduces failure modes during spacecraft inspection. Existing planners rely on line-of-sight inspection metrics which perform occlusion checks against a known target and conflate geometric visibility with task-relevant information. articles.title: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?
articles.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can often tell when they are being tested. This ability, known as evaluation awareness, can lead models to act more cautiously during safety evaluations than in real use. Existing work has studied evaluation awareness almost entirely in English, although models serve users in many languages. articles.title: KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents
articles.summary: Deep search agents solve knowledge-intensive tasks through long-horizon, multi-turn interactions, where assigning credit to individual search decisions is fundamentally difficult. Outcome-based reinforcement learning provides only a single terminal reward shared across an entire trajectory. articles.title: Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models
articles.summary: Continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs) offer an alternative approach to parallel language generation; however, most existing studies directly use transformer architectures from either causal large language models (LLMs) or Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) for image generation, which were not optimized for CDLMs. In this paper, we conduct a systematic study on Transformer architectures for CDLMs and introduce Language Diffusion Transformer (LangDiT), combining feature and query-key normalizati

articles.title: ACEdit: Stable Multi-Turn Image Editing via Asymmetric Conditioning
articles.summary: Image editing models produce impressive results for individual edits, but their quality often deteriorates over multiple editing turns. Each editing turn introduces small distribution shifts that accumulate over successive edits, creating a gap between the input distributions encountered during the editor's original training and multi-turn inference. articles.title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning
articles.summary: Time Series Language Models (TSLMs) enable language-based understanding and reasoning over temporal data, yet a fundamental question remains: what information should their time-series representations preserve, and what variation should they factor out? Existing TSLMs typically expose the language model to a single representation, imposing a fixed inductive bias across downstream tasks. articles.title: Dense4D: Pixel-Level 4D Human Correspondence
articles.summary: Reconstructing human motion in 4D requires identifying the same surface points through articulation, deformation and changes in visibility. We introduce Dense4D, to our knowledge the first feed-forward model dedicated to dense 4D correspondence across the body, clothing and hair from a set of monocular RGB images, without a body template. articles.title: Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas
articles.summary: One of the first steps of a research pipeline is generating ideas. Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate this step, but most of this work optimizes the quality of individual ideas, while overlooking diversity. articles.title: Mem4Act: Learning Effective Latent Memory for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
articles.summary: Long-horizon robotic manipulation fundamentally requires memory: agents must retain task-relevant information from past observations and interactions and use it to guide future actions. articles.title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
articles.summary: The capabilities of an agent swarm depend on both its individual members and how they coordinate. Yet existing multi-agent systems often train agents within fixed orchestration structures, separating the learning of individual capabilities from the organization of collective behavior. articles.title: AVC-Reward: Event-Centric Audio-Video Consistency Evaluation
articles.summary: As joint audio-video generation models become more capable, they can generate audio-visual scenes exhibiting three forms of complexity: multi-event composition, multi-layer audio mixture, and asymmetric cross-modal relations. articles.title: Not Just a Subject: Capturing Adaptive Scene-Specific Variance for Visual Storytelling
articles.summary: Recent advancements in diffusion models have significantly improved text-to-image generation, enabling their application to visual storytelling, where coherent image sequences are generated from narrative prompts. articles.title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
articles.summary: Large language model (LLM)-based agents and multi-agent systems increasingly tackle complex tasks through long-horizon tool use and inter-agent collaboration. However, these systems are prone to deviating from the overall goal as execution unfolds, which wastes execution resources and leads to undesired outcomes, a failure termed goal drift. articles.title: Magna: simulating magic state factories as cheaply as Clifford circuits
articles.summary: Classical simulation of magic state factories, including distillation, cultivation, and code switching, is challenging because of their substantial non-Clifford content. articles.title: MindEval2: Clinically Grounded Patients and Rubrics for Evaluating Language Models in Mental Health Support
articles.summary: With people increasingly turning to AI chatbots for mental health support, the need to evaluate these tools is becoming more pressing. Recent benchmarks attempt to mimic a realistic setting by simulating multi-turn interactions with synthetic patients and evaluating them with an LLM-as-a-judge. articles.title: Grid-Bench: Can LLMs Predict How Discrete Worlds Change?
articles.summary: Spatial instructions describe how to move objects, transform regions, or modify their surroundings. When several operations are applied in sequence, each acts on a configuration shaped by earlier changes. How accurately can large language models (LLMs) predict the resulting spatial state? articles.title: Velox: Spatial Memory Makes World Models Efficient
articles.summary: Video world models turn actions and camera motion into long visual rollouts, making video a natural interface for interactive simulation. Such interaction requires responsive generation, yet coherent rollouts must retain visual memory of what has already been generated. Chunked video diffusion models usually keep this context in growing KV caches, so later chunks become progressively slower. articles.title: TraHist: Fast and Accurate Cardinality Estimation for Trajectory Data (Extended Version)
articles.summary: Cardinality estimation is fundamental for query optimization in database systems. Histogram-based estimators are widely used for their simplicity and efficiency but rely on point-centric partitioning that assumes record independence. articles.title: From picometre displacements to a three-dimensional lattice gas of polar skyrmions
articles.summary: Polar skyrmions, the electric analogues of magnetic skyrmions, form arrays in PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices that are known to be only short-range ordered, but how this disordered ensemble is organized in three dimensions, and how its microscopic structure underlies this organization, have remained largely inaccessible. articles.title: Classical Capacity of Single-Mode Bosonic Gaussian Channels
articles.summary: The classical capacity of a noisy optical channel is the maximum rate at which information can be transmitted reliably, given a constraint on the mean input energy. articles.summary: Moiré semiconductors provide a physical realization of the Hubbard model. Bandwidth-tuned Mott transitions and complex phase diagrams mimicking those of high-temperature superconductors have been demonstrated near a weak Mott insulating state at half-band-filling. articles.title: ARC-SORT: Adaptive, Robust, Compensated Multi-Object Tracking with Interacting Multiple Models
articles.summary: Multi-object tracking in sports broadcasts is hard for two reasons: athletes move fast and change direction abruptly, and the camera pans and zooms at the same time. We present ARC-SORT (Adaptive, Robust, Compensated SORT), a tracking-by-detection tracker that trains nothing and runs in real time. articles.title: Chemical Demographics of Star-forming Regions
